grammar.gloss: The form on every verb card is a tense — the casual twin of ます.
An ichidan verb drops る and adds ない. する → しない, 来る → こない.
One rule for all eight endings — く→かない, む→まない. う→わない, and ある→ない.
ない is an i-adjective, so the plain past is the かった rule you already have.
The plain past is the te-form with て swapped for た, で for だ.
The plain copula. だった, じゃない, じゃなかった — and never after an i-adjective.
The casual yes and no. A plain question drops か and rises instead.
Have ever done it — an experience, not an event that happened.
Some of the things you do, not all of them and not in order. It ends in する.
Please don't — the ない form in the slot where ～てください takes the te-form.
X is Y — the fundamental copula.
Confirmation / softening (\"It is, isn't it?\")
I came from ~ (origin pattern)

あまり and ぜんぜん require a negative verb ending (～ません)
Please do ~. Ichidan verbs drop る and add て.
A verb ending in く takes いて; ぐ takes いで.
The largest group — う, つ and る all become って.
む, ぬ and ぶ all become んで; す becomes して.
Doing it now, or doing it as a rule.
Did ~. Swap ます for ました; every verb behaves the same way.
Did not ~. ません picks up でした behind it.
Was ~. Nouns and na-adjectives swap です for でした.
Was ~. An i-adjective drops い and takes かった — never でした.
How was ~?
Makes a noun out of a verb — 食べる becomes 食べ物, the thing you eat.
Counter for cupfuls and bowlfuls. The sound changes at one, three and six.
Not very ~. The polite way to say something was bad.
The verb for wearing changes with where the thing goes — shoulders down, waist down, or on your head.
A colour is a noun and an adjective — 赤いかばん describes the bag, かばんは赤です names the colour.
